title: API gateway rate limiter admits bursts and leaks memory
issue:
Incident report: our API gateway's `ratelimit.RateLimiter` lets clients exceed their quota (bursts pass right after a window boundary, and some requests slip through under concurrent load), and gateway memory grows without bound because it keeps state for every client key it has ever seen.

Replace it with a correct token-bucket limiter. The public API is fixed and documented in `README.md`; callers depend on it:

- `RateLimiter(rate, capacity, clock=None, max_keys=10_000, idle_ttl=300.0)`. `rate` (tokens/second, float) must be > 0 and `capacity` (int) >= 1, otherwise `ValueError`. `clock` is a zero-argument callable returning seconds (default `time.monotonic`).
- Each key has a bucket that starts full and refills continuously at `rate` tokens per second up to `capacity`. Fractional refill counts.
- `allow(key, cost=1) -> bool` atomically consumes `cost` tokens if available and returns True, otherwise returns False and consumes nothing. `cost` must be an int in `1..capacity`, otherwise `ValueError`.
- `retry_after(key, cost=1) -> float` returns the seconds until `cost` tokens will be available (0.0 if available now). It does not consume tokens.
- Thread safety: concurrent callers must never be admitted beyond what the bucket allows.
- Memory: never hold more than `max_keys` buckets; when full, evict the least recently used key. A bucket untouched for `idle_ttl` seconds or more must be dropped no later than the next call to `allow`. `len(limiter)` returns the number of buckets currently held.
- The clock can jump backwards (NTP corrections). That must never raise and must never grant extra tokens, including after the clock moves forward again.
